passages.note: Final-reading vote page; shows Kolodin's Aye vote but no provision text.
Bill status page lists Kolodin as prime sponsor of HB2394; signed by governor 05/21/2024.

passages.provision_quote: A candidate for public office or political party office who will appear on the ballot in this state or any citizen of this state may bring an action for digital impersonation within two years after the date that the person knows, or in the exercise of reasonable diligence should know, that a digital impersonation of the person who is bringing the action was published.
passages.note: Enacted statute text (16-1023); creates a private civil action against a digital impersonation's creator/publisher and expressly exempts interactive computer service providers from liability.

rows.reasoning: HB2394 is a narrowly-tailored civil tort for deepfake "digital impersonation" of candidates and others: it creates a private right of action against the creator/funder of the impersonation, expressly exempts "a provider of an interactive computer service" from liability for third-party content, and directs the section be "narrowly construed in favor of both free and open discourse." It neither requires platforms to remove or label false information, nor endorses voluntary standards, nor bans government (court) involvement in the resulting relief. It does not establish any of the five rungs on platform/government responsibility for combating online misinformation broadly, so it is adjacent rather than on-question.
